evidence: Both import cycles are gone (cycles detector reports no open issues).
GPUtil was removed from pyproject and from all GPU discovery paths; nvidia-smi and rocm-smi are the only backends.
The dependency set is focused: httpx, pydantic-settings, FastAPI/uvicorn, Typer/Rich, structlog, numpy, psutil.
No duplicate HTTP client or settings framework was found.
requirements.txt now mirrors pyproject and no longer lists GPUtil; the dependency lists cannot drift silently.
uv.lock is committed (63 packages), pinning transitive versions.
dependency_health.issues_preventing_higher_score: Dependencies are focused and locked; the remaining gap is automation that regenerates uv.lock when pyproject changes.

dependency_health.dimension_character: Dependencies now have clear roles and the two maintenance hazards (unmaintained GPUtil and import cycles) are gone. The declared set is small, though the legacy requirements.txt has drifted from pyproject.
dependency_health.score_rationale: GPUtil and both import cycles are gone, requirements.txt mirrors pyproject and uv.lock pins the resolved graph. A CI lock-drift check is the remaining polish.

issues.summary: No CI check keeps uv.lock in sync with pyproject
issues.suggestion: Add a CI step that runs uv lock --check (or uv sync --frozen) and fails on drift.
evidence: uv.lock is committed but nothing enforces regeneration when direct dependencies change.
A stale lock file silently defeats the reproducibility goal.

add.description: One HTTP client (httpx), one settings stack (pydantic-settings) and one CLI/UI stack (Typer/Rich + FastAPI) avoid duplicate-purpose libraries.
